The claim: stick divided into parts of lengths 1, 2, 4, ..., 2^n. There are n+1 parts. All 2^{n+1} subset sums are pairwise distinct. This is the standard fact that binary representations are unique. Subset sums of powers of 2 are distinct because each integer from 0 to 2^{n+1}-1 has a unique binary representation. So the claim is true.

Proof sketch: Suppose two subsets give the same sum. Their difference gives a sum of ±1·2^i terms equal to zero; take the smallest power with nonzero coefficient, say 2^k, then the sum is 2^k (odd multiple of 2^k) plus multiples of higher powers which are divisible by 2^{k+1}, so total is divisible by 2^k but not 2^{k+1}, hence nonzero — contradiction.

Claim is true. Witness: none, so witness_valid is null.
